+//! The tool's share of an operation's generation stamp: the library
+//! tool's name, kind and every number its kind reads, and its modelled
+//! body's envelope. Split out of `stamp` along the tool seam (#532),
+//! unchanged - the bytes written are the ones `current_stamp` always
+//! wrote, so no stored stamp moves.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own staleness design (see `stamp`).
+
+use std::hash::Hasher;
+
+use flecs_ecs::prelude::World;
+
+use crate::model;
+
+use super::OpParams;
+
+/// Write the tool named `tool_name` into `h`. `None` when the tool is
+/// gone - an unresolvable digest is never equal to a stored one.
+pub(super) fn write(world: &World, tool_name: &str, params: &OpParams, h: &mut std::hash::DefaultHasher) -> Option<()> {
+    let w = |h: &mut std::hash::DefaultHasher, v: f64| h.write(&v.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
+    h.write(tool_name.as_bytes());
+    h.write_u8(0xff);
+    let tool_entity = model::find_by_name(world, tool_name)?;
+    let tool = model::tool_of(world, &tool_entity)?;
+    h.write_u8(match tool.kind {
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::EndMill => 0,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::BallNose => 1,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::BullNose => 2,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Drill => 3,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Tap => 4,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Bore => 5,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Turning => 6,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Groove => 7,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Thread => 8,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Form => 9,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Taper => 10,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Probe => 11,
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Torch => 12,
+    });
+    for v in [
+        tool.diameter,
+        tool.corner_r,
+        // The nose circle rides the digest from its first build
+        // (M5.2 A): it is the envelope ball, so an edit re-marks the
+        // verdict Stale through here, exactly like the diameter does.
+        tool.nose_radius,
+        tool.flute_len,
+        tool.shank_d,
+        tool.shank_len,
+        tool.holder_d,
+        tool.holder_len,
+    ] {
+        w(h, v);
+    }
+    // Kind-scoped numbers: a tool digests only what its kind reads. A
+    // tip_angle parked on a ball nose is inert data, and inert data must
+    // never make an operation look stale - the same law the profile and
+    // the cycles draw by. It also keeps every pre-M1.6 stamp value
+    // unchanged: no one-time churn for the milling kinds.
+    // The blade's width rides the digest from its first build
+    // (M5.2 C): the kerf's width IS the tool, so a re-ground blade
+    // is a different cut - marked Stale through here, never through
+    // the params stamp, which never reads it.
+    match tool.kind {
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Drill => w(h, tool.tip_angle),
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Tap => w(h, tool.pitch),
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Groove => w(h, tool.width),
+        // The threading insert digests BOTH its profile numbers
+        // (M5.2 D): the crest width and the flanks' angle are the
+        // wave's footprint - a recut V is a different thread even
+        // when the operation's pitch and depth never moved.
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Thread => {
+            w(h, tool.width);
+            w(h, tool.tip_angle);
+        }
+        // The gauge digests its band width - the kerf's span, the
+        // blade's law - and its crown needs no line here: the arc
+        // radius rides the global nose_radius row above, read at
+        // the gate that makes it mean anything (M5.2 E2).
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Form => w(h, tool.width),
+        // The chamfer mill digests its cone angle from its first
+        // build (M2.4 B): the congruence door reads it against the
+        // face's angle, so a re-cut cone is a different chamfer even
+        // when width, depth and the wall itself never moved.
+        crate::tools::ToolKind::Taper => w(h, tool.tip_angle),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+    // A Thread OP times its helix against the TOOL's pitch (M2.4 C, the
+    // tap cycle's reading), whatever kind carries it - so the clause
+    // belongs to the operation, not the tool kind: the turning thread
+    // insert's pitch stays inert there (that ride reads pitch from
+    // params), and no pre-M2.4-C digest changes, because only the new
+    // operation kinds reach past this line.
+    if matches!(params, OpParams::Thread { .. }) {
+        w(h, tool.pitch);
+    }
+    // M11.3: a tool that may not plunge into solid changes the entries;
+    // a byte only then, so no centre-cutting op's digest moves.
+    if !tool.center_cutting {
+        h.write_u8(0xCC);
+    }
+    // #368: a modelled body's envelope - bytes only when there is one,
+    // so no digest without a body moves.
+    crate::tool_body::digest(world, &tool_entity, h);
+    Some(())
+}

+//! The wire EDM contour's stored parameters (#532, part of #290): the
+//! two planes of the workpiece, the machine condition the cut burns
+//! with (by the control's own id), the stated punch / die side and the
+//! start hole - resolved into the motion crate's `wire_edm::WireParams`
+//! at generation. The wire's diameter and the spark gap are NOT stored
+//! here: the machine's condition table is their one source (#531).
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own parameter set over the umbrella's decisions
+//! (#290 D2, D4, D8) and general wire EDM practice (see
+//! `motion::wire_edm`); no vendor material consulted.
+
+use super::height::Height;
+
+pub use crate::wire_edm::WireSide;
+
+/// The longest condition id an operation stores (a control's selector
+/// is a short word; this only bounds a hand-edited file).
+pub const CONDITION_ID_MAX: usize = 64;
+
+/// The wire contour's parameters.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireContourOp {
+    /// The workpiece's top: the plane the profile is read on (the upper
+    /// programmed plane a taper will pose toward, #536).
+    pub top_z: Height,
+    /// The workpiece's bottom: the lower programmed plane the moves
+    /// ride (#290 D2).
+    pub bottom_z: Height,
+    /// The machine's EDM condition this cut burns with, by its id; the
+    /// empty word is "none chosen", refused at the command door.
+    pub condition: String,
+    /// Which side of the profile is the product - stated by the user,
+    /// never inferred from the geometry (#290 D8).
+    pub side: WireSide,
+    /// The start hole / threading point, world XY mm; `None` is not
+    /// stated, and a closed profile is refused at generation without it.
+    pub start: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+    /// The constant taper (#536), degrees from vertical: 0 is a
+    /// vertical cut; positive widens the profile downward from the top
+    /// plane (a die's relief, a drafted punch's base), negative narrows
+    /// it. The machine's `edm.max_taper_deg` bounds it at generation.
+    pub taper_deg: f64,
+    /// The 4-axis cut (#537): `Some` reads the selection as two closed
+    /// profiles - the upper on the top plane, the lower on the bottom
+    /// plane - and pairs them into rulings by the stated rule. `None`
+    /// is the one-profile cut.
+    pub four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>,
+}
+
+/// How the two profiles of a 4-axis cut are paired (#537) - stated,
+/// never inferred.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum WirePairingRule {
+    /// By normalised arc length, each profile walked counter-clockwise
+    /// from its point nearest the start hole.
+    ArcLength,
+    /// By the stated sync pairs, normalised arc length between them.
+    SyncPoints,
+}
+
+/// One sync pair, world XY mm: a point of the upper profile and the
+/// point of the lower profile the same ruling passes through. A side
+/// left `None` is an unpaired sync point - storable (a pick in
+/// progress), refused by name at generation.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireSyncPair {
+    pub upper: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+    pub lower: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+}
+
+/// The most sync pairs an operation stores (bounds a hand-edited file).
+pub const SYNC_PAIRS_MAX: usize = 4096;
+/// The 4-axis tolerance a new cut starts with, mm.
+pub const FOUR_AXIS_TOLERANCE: f64 = 0.05;
+
+/// The 4-axis cut's stored parameters (#537).
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireFourAxis {
+    pub pairing: WirePairingRule,
+    /// The sync pairs; read only when the pairing is by sync points.
+    pub sync: Vec<WireSyncPair>,
+    /// The most (mm) the wire may stand off the profiles past the kerf
+    /// offset to keep its kerf out of a twisted ruled surface
+    /// (`motion::wire_edm::ruled`).
+    pub tolerance: f64,
+}
+
+impl Default for WireFourAxis {
+    fn default() -> Self {
+        WireFourAxis { pairing: WirePairingRule::ArcLength, sync: Vec::new(), tolerance: FOUR_AXIS_TOLERANCE }
+    }
+}
+
+impl WireFourAxis {
+    fn is_sane(&self) -> bool {
+        let pt = |q: Option<[f64; 2]>| q.is_none_or(|s| s.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite() && v.abs() < 1e9));
+        self.tolerance.is_finite()
+            && (0.0..=10.0).contains(&self.tolerance)
+            && self.sync.len() <= SYNC_PAIRS_MAX
+            && self.sync.iter().all(|s| pt(s.upper) && pt(s.lower))
+    }
+}
+
+impl WireContourOp {
+    /// Structural sanity (no world): the heights, a finite start point
+    /// and a condition id that is one short word. Whether the machine
+    /// states that condition is the command door's question
+    /// (`operation::wire_op::condition_of`).
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn is_sane(&self) -> bool {
+        self.top_z.is_sane()
+            && self.bottom_z.is_sane()
+            && self.start.is_none_or(|s| s.iter().all(|v| v.is_finite() && v.abs() < 1e9))
+            && self.taper_deg.is_finite()
+            && self.taper_deg.abs() < 90.0
+            && self.four_axis.as_ref().is_none_or(WireFourAxis::is_sane)
+            && self.condition.len() <= CONDITION_ID_MAX
+            && !self.condition.chars().any(char::is_control)
+    }
+}

+//! The wire contour's file mirror (#532): the op's parameters as plain
+//! keys - the two workpiece planes, the machine condition's id, the
+//! side and the start hole. `side` has no default on purpose: a file
+//! (or an MCP patch) that leaves it out is refused, never read as a
+//! die - the side is stated, not inferred (#290 D8); the 4-axis block's
+//! pairing rule (#537) likewise. The wire and the
+//! gap are not here: they are the machine's condition table's.
+//! Provenance: our own file format (`project/mod.rs`); the names are ours.
+
+use super::*;
+
+use crate::operation::{WireContourOp, WireFourAxis, WirePairingRule, WireSide, WireSyncPair, FOUR_AXIS_TOLERANCE};
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum WireSideDto {
+    Die,
+    Punch,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireContourDto {
+    pub top_z: HeightDto,
+    pub bottom_z: HeightDto,
+    /// The machine's EDM condition id; absent is none chosen.
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
+    pub condition: String,
+    pub side: WireSideDto,
+    /// The start hole / threading point, `[x, y]` mm; absent is not
+    /// stated.
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub start: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+    /// The constant taper, degrees (#536); absent is a vertical cut, so
+    /// every file written before it reads unchanged.
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_zero")]
+    pub taper_deg: f64,
+    /// The 4-axis cut (#537); absent is the one-profile cut, so every
+    /// file written before it reads unchanged.
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub four_axis: Option<WireFourAxisDto>,
+}
+
+/// The pairing rule's words. No default: a 4-axis block that leaves the
+/// rule out is refused, never read as arc length (#537: stated).
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum WirePairingDto {
+    ArcLength,
+    SyncPoints,
+}
+
+/// One sync pair, `[x, y]` mm each; a side left out is unpaired (kept,
+/// and refused by name at generation).
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireSyncDto {
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub upper: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub lower: Option<[f64; 2]>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireFourAxisDto {
+    pub pairing: WirePairingDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
+    pub sync: Vec<WireSyncDto>,
+    /// The twist tolerance, mm; absent is the default.
+    #[serde(default = "four_axis_tolerance")]
+    pub tolerance: f64,
+}
+
+fn four_axis_tolerance() -> f64 {
+    FOUR_AXIS_TOLERANCE
+}
+
+#[allow(clippy::trivially_copy_pass_by_ref)]
+fn is_zero(v: &f64) -> bool {
+    *v == 0.0
+}
+
+impl WireContourDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_op(p: &WireContourOp) -> Self {
+        WireContourDto {
+            top_z: p.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: p.bottom_z.into(),
+            condition: p.condition.clone(),
+            side: match p.side {
+                WireSide::Die => WireSideDto::Die,
+                WireSide::Punch => WireSideDto::Punch,
+            },
+            start: p.start,
+            taper_deg: p.taper_deg,
+            four_axis: p.four_axis.as_ref().map(|f| WireFourAxisDto {
+                pairing: match f.pairing {
+                    WirePairingRule::ArcLength => WirePairingDto::ArcLength,
+                    WirePairingRule::SyncPoints => WirePairingDto::SyncPoints,
+                },
+                sync: f.sync.iter().map(|s| WireSyncDto { upper: s.upper, lower: s.lower }).collect(),
+                tolerance: f.tolerance,
+            }),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn to_params(&self) -> OpParams {
+        OpParams::WireContour(WireContourOp {
+            top_z: self.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: self.bottom_z.into(),
+            condition: self.condition.clone(),
+            side: match self.side {
+                WireSideDto::Die => WireSide::Die,
+                WireSideDto::Punch => WireSide::Punch,
+            },
+            start: self.start,
+            taper_deg: self.taper_deg,
+            four_axis: self.four_axis.as_ref().map(|f| WireFourAxis {
+                pairing: match f.pairing {
+                    WirePairingDto::ArcLength => WirePairingRule::ArcLength,
+                    WirePairingDto::SyncPoints => WirePairingRule::SyncPoints,
+                },
+                sync: f.sync.iter().map(|s| WireSyncPair { upper: s.upper, lower: s.lower }).collect(),
+                tolerance: f.tolerance,
+            }),
+        })
+    }
+}

+## #1164 - Wire EDM: taper by angle word (control-computed lean)
+
+#536 posted a constant taper as U/V moves and refused angle-word controls by not offering them: with an angle word the control decides the lean at corners and lead-ins, which the wire laws could not see. This adds the dialect with that decision stated as machine data.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **The dialect is machine data: `edm.taper_angle`, an object of two enumerated words with no default.** `positive` (`top_left` / `top_right`): the side of the direction of travel a positive angle word leans the wire's top toward. `corner` (`mitre` / `cone`): what the control cuts at a corner. Stating the object is stating the dialect: the post writes the angle word and no U/V. A garbled word refuses the file; an unstated one is refused by name at generation ("states no edm.taper_angle.corner (mitre or cone)"), never guessed. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`, beside the existing `taper_on` / `taper_off`; each missing code refuses by name. A machine stating neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name, and the refusal names both.
+- **The generator and the verify model the stated rule; the post writes only what the control reads.** `mitre`: the sides keep their planes and meet along the mitre - #536's path exactly (its CL golden byte for byte, pinned). `cone`: the wire pivots about each top-plane corner with its lean held at the angle, the lower end on an arc of radius `H tan(angle)`; the CL lays it as posed turning moves at most 2 degrees apart (each chord within `|d| (1 - cos 1 deg)`, 1.5e-4 of the lean offset - 0.1 um on the fixture) so the #534/#536 wire laws read it at every height like any lean. The post drops the turning moves (the control makes them) and writes each move's X Y on the programmed plane.
+- **The programmed plane is the work's top**, where the profile holds (#536) and the control pivots; the section's note says its Z (the control is set to it). The guides' U/V stroke check still runs on every pose, as the control still drives U/V.
+- **Lead-in and lead-out:** the post writes `taper_on` and the angle word before the lead-in and `taper_off` before the lead-out, and the path models the control ramping the lean linearly over each of those moves - #536's lead-in twist and upright lead-out. Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name (the corner's turn would be cut by no move); move the start hole.
+- **The word's sign is computed from the path:** the side the top leans relative to the travel on every side move, the same everywhere (else refused), signed by `positive`.
+- **4-axis (#537) on an angle-word machine is refused by name** at generation and at the post: one angle cannot state different upper and lower profiles.
+- **U/V machines are unchanged:** the stamp, CL and NC of every U/V cut are byte-identical (the #536 and #537 goldens pass unedited).
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- **An `arc` corner rule with a stated radius** (the control rounds the lean change over a radius). A third value is cheap to add later; two rules cover the pinned cases and each value added needs its own model and pin.
+- **A default corner rule.** Guessing what the control cuts is exactly the silent motion #536 refused.
+- **Refusing sharp corners under any angle-word taper.** Safe but needless once the rule is stated and modelled.
+- **XY on the lower guide plane, as the U/V post.** The control's corner rule acts on its programmed contour; the profile and the pivot are on the top plane.
+
+**Not exercised on a real EDM control (D10).** The fixture's codes and words are invented; a user fills `edm.taper_angle` and `edm.codes.taper_angle` from their manual and dry-runs before any cut.
+
+**Sources:** plane trigonometry (a cone's section; the textbook mitre), #290 D2/D5/D7/D10, #536's decision record. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low - another corner value is one arm in `motion::wire_edm::taper` and one word in `post::machine::edm_taper`.

+## #532 - Wire EDM 2-axis contour op
+
+The umbrella (#290, D1-D10) decided the build order, the CL shape (D2: `to` on the lower programmed plane, no pose for a vertical cut), the condition table (D4) and that punch/die and the corner minimum belong to this op (D8). These are the points it left open.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **A wire cut mounts no library tool.** `KindInfo::tool_kinds` is the empty set for the wire family (`tool_law::NO_TOOL`, `KindInfo::mounts_tool`), the operation's `tool` is the empty word, and the command door refuses a wire cut that names one. The wire's diameter and the spark gap come from the machine's condition (#531) through `Edm::condition`, their only source; the stamp digests them in the tool's place, so an edited condition table re-marks the cut Stale.
+- **The side is stated; a reader never defaults it.** `side` is `die` (wire inside the profile) or `punch` (wire outside). The file and MCP shape has no serde default for it: a parameter object without `side` is refused. The in-app draft (`seed_wire_contour`) starts at `die`, as the umbrella's "explicit parameter with a default" says - and that draft cannot be created anyway until a condition is named.
+- **One closed profile per operation.** An open run, several rings, a crossing or area-less ring are refused by name. An open profile has no punch or die side; it is a follow-up issue, not a guess.
+- **Outside corners are mitred, not rolled.** The wire-centre path is `geo2d::Region::offset_sharp` (the existing clipper2 offsetter): at a corner the wire wraps around, the path is the sharp intersection of the two parallels, so the wire stays at or beyond the kerf offset and the product's corner stays sharp. Past the offsetter's mitre limit (corners sharper than about 60 degrees) the join is squared, still no nearer than the offset.
+- **Inside corners: the cover law, 2 um.** A corner is "too tight" when some point of the profile stands farther than `wire radius + gap + 0.002 mm` from the wire-centre path - the rolling-circle reading of "minimum internal radius is wire radius + gap". It also catches a slot, notch or neck under the kerf width. The refusal names the spot, the minimum radius and its two terms.
+- **The profile is judged as given.** It is a polygon (picked edges or the model's through-silhouette). A round drawn with facets turning more than about 17 degrees reads as a row of sharp inside corners at a 0.165 mm offset and is refused; a finer model is the fix.
+- **No arc fitting.** The path is straight moves: the exact mitred parallel of the polygon, on the offsetter's 1 nm lattice. Fitting arcs would move the path by a facet's sagitta, more than the cover law's tolerance.
+- **Start hole and leads.** Every closed profile needs a stated start hole / threading point, a punch included (a hole or the stock's edge outside the profile). It must stand on the waste side at least the kerf offset from the profile. The lead-in is the straight line from it to the nearest point of the wire path (it meets a straight side square); the profile is cut counter-clockwise from there; the lead-out retraces the lead-in back to the threading point. No lead length or shape parameter exists yet.
+- **Where the refusals stand.** A missing condition, gap or wire diameter: at command creation (create, paste, edit, retype). A missing or misplaced start hole and the corner minimum: at generation, where the profile is read. So an operation can be created first and its start hole placed after.
+- **Planes.** The op stores the workpiece top (where the profile is read) and bottom (the lower programmed plane the moves ride). It has no clearance plane - a wire never lifts out of the work - and `OpParams::clearance()` answers the top for it.
+- **Moves.** All `Feed`, with no feed number (the control's generator sets the rate) and no pose. The path starts and ends at the threading point; there is no rapid.
+- **No CL format change.** The CL carries no wire record. The path's notes state the side, the offset's two terms, the kerf width and the threading point; the wire post (#533) can read the condition id and the start hole from the op's parameters, as the plasma post reads its op.
+- **Until the wire post exists** the program gate refuses a wire cut by name. The machine check on a wire EDM judges X/Y travel and names what it does not judge (wire sweep, slug, start-hole clearance: #534).
+- **A minimal op page ships here.** The UI's registry-wide tab law draws every kind's sections and fails a kind whose tabs are empty, so `wire_page.rs` gives the Wire Contour its fields: side and start hole on Geometry, the two planes on Heights, the condition (a list of what the op's machine states) on Passes, and no Feeds tab. Picking the start hole in the viewport, the kind's own glyph and the ribbon's behaviour on a wire EDM document stay #535's.
+- **`stamp_tool.rs`.** The tool's share of the stamp moved out of `stamp.rs` unchanged, so the wire branch fits without growing that file; no stored stamp of a tool-mounting op moves.
+
+**Why:** Prime Directive - correct or refused by name. A second statement of the wire's diameter (a tool beside the condition) could disagree with the first; a defaulted side scraps a part; a rounded or arc-fitted path is not "offset by exactly the kerf".
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- A `ToolKind::Wire` library tool: a second source for the wire diameter, plus a tool editor page before any wire op could be made.
+- Rolling the wire around outside corners (round joins): the offsetter flattens that arc to 5 um chords, which brings the wire up to 5 um nearer the corner than the offset.
+- Refusing a missing start hole at command creation: the profile is only read at generation, and the natural order is create, then place the hole.
+- A typed wire record in the CL (as plasma's `PlasmaCut`): a `.cl` format change with every reader and golden touched, for facts the post can read from the op.
+- Lead-in length, angle and arc leads, overlap past the entry point, cut direction as a parameter: none is in the issue, and none is needed for a correct cut.
+- Checking the condition's wire against the machine's `edm.wire_diameters` list: a contradiction inside the machine file, which is #531's file law, not this op's.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low for the parameters (the DTO is additive: leads, direction and corner style can join as optional keys); medium for the tool-less law (about a dozen doors read `mounts_tool`); a CL wire record, if #533 wants one, bumps the dump version and regenerates the two goldens.

+## #533 - Generic ISO-style wire EDM post (codes as machine data)
+
+The umbrella (#290) decided that dialects are data (D5): one generic post per EDM kind writes the RS-274 motion words itself and takes every EDM-specific code from the machine's `.mch` `edm.codes`, refusing by name when one is missing. #532 decided the path is the wire-centre path (kerf already in it) with no feed. These are the points this post settled.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **Compensation is cancelled, never engaged.** The Wire Contour's moves are the wire-centre path (#532 puts wire radius + gap in it). The post writes `edm.codes.comp_off` before every cut and never reads a left/right compensation code: a control offset on top of the CAM offset would double the kerf. `comp_off` is required for that reason - an unstated cancel could leave a previous program's offset active.
+- **Required codes.** Always `condition` and `comp_off`. With `edm.awt: true` also `thread`, `cut` and `tip_disposal`. Each missing one refuses the post as "machine <m> states no edm.codes.<x>". Without AWT (false or unstated: not claimed) the post writes ISO 6983 `M00` with a comment for the operator to thread at the start hole and to cut the wire at the end, so the AWT codes are not needed.
+- **The condition code is a template.** `edm.codes.condition` must hold `{id}`, which takes the op's condition id (`"FX-COND {id}"` -> `FX-COND C110`). A template with no `{id}` would select nothing and is refused by name. A condition id that is not one word (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`) is refused.
+- **Order in a section:** G0 to the start hole (the first cut's start, the threading point), thread, select the condition, cancel compensation, then the cut in X Y; after it, cut the wire and dispose of the tip. The program assumes the wire is NOT threaded at its start, and says so in its header comment. A rapid while threaded, a Z change (2-axis: one programmed plane), a posed move, an arc off the XY plane, a cycle, a tool change and a spindle speed are refused by name.
+- **No F word.** The generator's condition sets the cutting rate (#532: the moves carry no feed).
+- **Plain RS-274 / ISO 6983 words only:** `%` fences, G20/G21, G90, G17, the work-offset word, G0/G1/G2/G3 with incremental I J, M00/M01, M30. These were judged universal enough; the words D5 named as unsafe to default (G41/G42, G21/G22-style EDM meanings, threading and condition words) all come from `edm.codes`.
+- **The engine's door: `wireEdm = true`.** The wire stream carries `PARAM EdmCondition`; a script that does not declare `wireEdm` is refused by name (as `liveTooling`, `threadHands`), so no cutting post can post a wire path as a cut, whatever the picker shows. The tool-less refusal in `op_streams` stays for any other tool-less kind.
+- **Codes live on `Machine.edm_codes`, parsed by a new `edm_codes.rs`,** not inside #530's `Edm` struct: #530/#531 are still in review, and this keeps their files untouched. The mirror and `script_props` expose `machine.edm = { codes, awt }` and `machine.kind` for a wire or sinker EDM.
+- **Registry.** "Generic ISO Wire EDM" in `BUILTINS`, the one `WIRE_POSTS` entry: it serves `wire_edm` only, is the default post for a wire EDM, and no cutting post serves a wire EDM.
+
+**Why:** Prime Directive and D5 - a code the machine did not state is never guessed; the kerf is applied exactly once.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- Posting the part contour with control compensation (G41/G42-style codes and the kerf in a register): #532 already decided the CAM path carries the kerf; doing it twice, or re-deriving the part contour, is wrong output.
+- Defaulting M00/M30 from `edm.codes`: these are ISO 6983 program-control words, not EDM codes; requiring them would make every machine file restate the standard.
+- Making `tip_disposal` optional under AWT: the issue lists it with the AWT codes, and an unstated disposal is not "none".
+- Adding `codes` to `Edm` itself: the natural home, but it would edit files of two PRs still in rework. It can move there when they land (a field move, no file-format change).
+
+**Not exercised on a real EDM control (D10):** the golden is posted against the synthetic fixture `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch`, whose codes (`FX-...`) are invented. A user with a real machine fills `edm.codes` from its manual and dry-runs before any cut.

+## #534 - Wire EDM: verification of a 2-axis cut
+
+The umbrella (#290 D7) decided a 2.5D verify: the kerf region against the part section, the start hole's threading clearance through the full height, and slug analysis by region connectivity, every flag blocking the post. These are the points it left open.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **Judged at the post, live.** The laws (`sim::verify::wire`) run in the verification gate's own wire clause (`posting_wire.rs`), beside the plasma clause, over the cached path and the part and stock as they stand now. Every finding is a blocking problem; there is no warning tier. The not-judged line says the 3D stock sim did not run for the wire and names the piece each cut frees. *Dropped:* a generator-time verdict cached with the path - the plasma precedent and the live-gate law (fixtures, machine limits) judge what the room is now.
+- **The whole height the wire passes.** A vertical wire cuts everything between its guides, so the heights judged span the op's planes, the part and the stock, whichever reaches farther: both ends (1 um inside, so a horizontal face is never sliced edge-on) and about every 2 mm between, at most nine sections. *Dropped:* the two programmed planes only - a part taller than the planes, or a step between them, would pass unseen.
+- **The kerf law is exact distance, not area.** A move gouges when its segment comes nearer the product's section than the kerf offset (less 0.1 um) or stands in it; the first such move is named with its depth, the spot and the count. *Dropped:* a swept-capsule boolean with an area threshold - a 10 um intrusion along a 1 mm move falls under any sensible sliver area.
+- **What "the part" is, by the stated side.** A punch's product is the model. A die's product is the model when the start hole stands outside it (a die plate: the opening is its hole); when the start hole stands in the model, the model is the opening itself (#532's whole-model die, where the model's silhouette is the profile) and the product is the stock around it. The start hole is stated and the generator already refuses it on the product's side, so this reads a stated fact, not the geometry's guess. *Dropped:* refusing the whole-model die - #532 ships it as the way a die is cut from a model.
+- **Threading clearance = the kerf offset.** The op states a threading point, not a hole diameter (#532), so "too small" is read as: the product stands nearer the threading point than wire radius + gap at some height. A start hole not stated, or a path that no longer starts at it, is refused by name. A pre-drilled hole's diameter is not modelled.
+- **The slug, by connectivity.** The kerf (the disc of the offset swept along the whole path) is taken out of the material section (stock and part); a piece left inside the kerf's filled outline is freed. A die's freed piece must hold none of the product (else "the part drops"); a punch's freed pieces must hold some (else "only waste drops"); a cut that frees nothing is refused (no stock around a die plate's hole means the slug cannot be judged - said, not passed).
+- **No capture or tab law yet.** D6 says an unsupported slug is refused unless a tab or capture is set; tabs are #539 and no capture parameter exists. This PR flags only a slug on the wrong side and a cut that frees nothing; a correct die or punch passes, and the report names what drops so the operator can catch it. When #539 lands it adds the capture law here.
+- **No part, no verdict.** A wire cut taken from the stock has no part to judge the kerf against and is refused at the gate by name.
+
+**Cost to change later:** the laws are pure functions of a path, an offset, a side, a start and a list of sections; adding the taper (#536) means a section pair per move and the ruled surface between, without changing the gate seam.

+
+The umbrella (#290) decided the taper is the move's pose (D2: `to` on the lower programmed plane, the pose the wire's direction toward the upper guide, both ends interpolating - the ruled surface), the taper words are machine data (D5), and the verify judges the ruled surface at every height and the angle and U/V against the machine (D7). These are the points it left open.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **One signed angle, `taper_deg`, on the Wire Contour.** 0 is the vertical cut; the DTO omits it at 0, so every file written before reads unchanged and a vertical cut's stamp, CL and NC are byte-identical (pinned). Positive widens the profile downward from the top plane - the die's relief and the drafted punch's base, both the common case; negative narrows it.
+- **The profile holds on the top plane.** #532 reads the profile on the top plane; the taper keeps it there and leans the wire below it. The kerf is measured across the leaning wire, so the horizontal offset on the top plane is `(wire radius + gap) / cos(angle)`, and every law of the vertical cut (cover, start hole, kerf) runs on that top-plane path unchanged. A corner refusal on a tapered cut therefore quotes the lean-scaled (horizontal) wire radius and gap.

Every pose is checked against the machine's maximum, not only the stated angle. A side the lean folds over, or a turn sharper than about 140 degrees, is refused by name.
+- **Upright at the start hole.** The wire is threaded vertical; the lead-in leans it to the first pose (a ruled twist the verify reads) and the lead-out stands it upright again with an explicit vertical pose, so the stream commands the return.
+- **Refusals and where they stand.** The angle against `edm.max_taper_deg` (an unstated maximum refuses any taper - absent is not zero): at generation, naming the op and the angle. The U/V offset against the U and V strokes, the programmed plane outside the guides, no U/V axis, no guide planes: in the wire EDM machine check, which blocks the post. The guide planes are read in machine Z, moved by the work offset's Z, as the X/Y strokes are judged.
+- **The post writes UV, with codes from `edm.codes`.** The app turns each leaning move into the lower guide's X Y and the upper guide's offset (`PARAM WireU`/`WireV`), from the pose and the guide planes; the script writes `taper_on` before the first leaning move, `uv` (a template with `{u}` and `{v}`) on each, and `taper_off` once the wire is upright, before the cut. Each code missing refuses by name. The synthetic fixture states `FX-TAPER-ON`, `FX-TAPER-OFF` and `U{u} V{v}` (D10: invented, not any control's).
+- **Verify reads the lean only from a stated taper.** `WireJob.taper`: a cut stating a taper has its poses read as the wire's lean; any other posed move stays unreadable (the #534 refusal stands). At each judged height the wire's section is `to + t (z - z0)`, and the kerf's reach toward the product in direction `u` is `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)` - the ellipse the leaning kerf cuts from the plane. The slug is judged per height from the wire's own section.

+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- **Angle words (a control-side taper with left/right and an angle).** The control then decides the corner and the lead-in lean itself, which the wire laws cannot see - motion the verify never judged. Refused by not being offered: a machine that states only angle codes has no `uv` and the post refuses by name. A follow-up can add it once a corner mode is stated as machine data.
+- **The profile on the lower programmed plane.** It would make `to` the profile's own parallel, but #532 reads the profile on the top plane and the product's working edge (die land, punch face) is usually at the top.
+- **One kerf radius `k / cos(max lean)` everywhere in the verify.** It over-reads every straight side and refuses a correct cut; the directional reach is exact on sides and safe at corners.
+- **Separate swing moves at corners.** Not needed: mitred vertices keep each face planar with one pose per vertex.
+
+**Not exercised on a real EDM control (D10).** The goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture; a user with a real machine fills `edm.codes`, the guide planes, the maximum taper and the U/V strokes from its manual and dry-runs before any cut.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low for angle words (another branch in the script and a code list); variable taper and 4-axis (#537) are a pose per vertex already, so they reuse the verify and post seams unchanged.

+## #537 - Wire EDM: 4-axis different upper/lower profiles (ruled surface pairing)
+
+The umbrella (#290) decided the geometry (D2: `to` on the lower programmed plane, the pose the wire toward its upper point, both ends interpolating - the ruled surface) and #536 built the pose, the U/V post and the leaning-kerf verify. These are the points they left open.
+
+**Decided:**
+
+- **A `four_axis` block on the Wire Contour, absent by default.** `Some` reads the selection as two profiles; the DTO omits it when `None`, so every file, stamp, CL and NC of a one-profile cut is unchanged. Its `pairing` word has no default in the file: a block that leaves the rule out is refused, never read as arc length. A taper angle stated beside it is refused - the two profiles are the lean.
+- **The two profiles are two picks at two heights, each flat.** A face (its one outer ring) or a closed edge chain; the higher one is the upper profile. Each must lie on one horizontal plane, and those planes must be the op's top and bottom planes - refused by name otherwise, never extrapolated. A third pick, two at one height, a face with holes or a vertex pick is refused by name.
+- **The pairing rule is one monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors.** By arc length: one anchor, each profile's point nearest the start hole, both rings walked counter-clockwise at the same share of their own length. By sync points: each stated pair (a point on each profile, world XY) is an anchor, arc length between neighbours. A ruling is laid at every vertex of either ring, so both profiles are traced exactly and the wire between two rulings sweeps one bilinear patch - what the verify already reads from two poses. The path's note states the rule.
+- **Sync points.** A pair with one side unstated is storable (a pick in progress) and refused by name at generation; so is a point more than 0.01 mm off its profile, two pairs on one point, and pairs whose order on the upper profile is not their order on the lower ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"). A sync point at a sharp corner is carried to the mitred corner of the wire path (the point midway between its two nearest feet).
+- **Fold law.** Between consecutive rulings the lower end moves by `a`, the upper by `b`; where `a . b < 0` the wire's section stops advancing strictly inside the part height - a fold (two rulings meeting in a point is the anti-parallel case). Refused by name with the height. Ends at right angles turn back only on the plane itself: no fold, a quarter-turn twist the kerf law judges. A crossing law refuses a pairing whose section at a quarter height crosses itself.
+- **A straight wire cannot touch a twisted ruled surface along its whole height, so the offset is widened, never the kerf let in.** Where the profiles turn against each other, the wire at the kerf offset on both planes stands nearer the surface between them (the tangent plane of a non-developable ruled surface turns along the ruling). The generator reads the stated surface (the two profiles under the same rule) at 33 heights with #536's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)` and widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear everywhere; the note says how much then stands on the profile planes. More than the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm) is refused by name with the spot. A constant taper needs exactly #536's `1 / cos(angle)`, so two profiles of a constant taper with sync pairs at the corners give #536's CL byte for byte (pinned).
+- **Machine limits reuse #536.** Every ruling's lean against `edm.max_taper_deg` at generation (unstated refuses); the U/V stroke, the U/V axes, the guide planes and the guides' reach in the wire EDM machine check, which reads poses and so needed no change.
+- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's (`WireJob.taper`); the kerf, threading and slug laws run at every judged height on the wire's own section. A ruling whose kerf burns the model blocks the post (pinned on a stepped part whose end faces are the two profiles).
+- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; the script treats it as a tapered section without an angle - the same `taper_on`, `uv`, `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes`, each missing one refused by name - and names the cut in a comment.
+- **No new command.** The block is an operation parameter: `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the MCP parameter patch carry it through the same JSON door. The page edits the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- **Offsetting each profile by the kerf and pairing the offsets, with no widening.** What a twisted surface gets is a gouge of `k (1 - cos(twist / 2))` between the planes - about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf. Small, silent and wrong: refused by the Prime Directive.
+- **A per-ruling offset** (widen only where the surface twists). Closer to the profiles, but a variable offset no longer traces a parallel of either profile and needs its own corner law. The uniform widening is safe everywhere and its cost is stated; a follow-up issue holds the refinement.
+- **`a . b <= 0` as the fold.** It refused every pair of rectangles of different aspect under arc length (their corners pass at right angles); the right-angle case is a twist, judged by the kerf law and the tolerance.
+- **Profiles at heights other than the op's planes, extrapolated.** The ruled surface outside the two profiles is nobody's statement.
+- **A fan (one point of a profile paired with a span of the other).** Two sync pairs on one point are refused; a follow-up can offer it as its own stated form.
+- **Inferring sync points from corners.** A pairing is stated, not guessed.
+
+**Not exercised on a real EDM control (D10).** The goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture. The verify judges the mesh as it stands: a model whose tessellation of a twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface between the two profiles is refused as a gouge (safe, and stricter than the model's own chord tolerance) - a follow-up issue holds a stated verify tolerance for that case.
+
+**Sources:** Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surfaces between two parametrised curves; chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", Computer-Aided Design 27(12), 1995 (a cylinder against a twisted ruled surface). No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted.
+
+**Cost to change later:** low for the per-ruling offset and the fan (inside `motion::wire_edm::ruled`); the stored block is additive, so open profiles (#1147) and skims (#538) can reuse the pairing unchanged.
